newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Chicago's surprise rise keeps European feeds calm.
newsitem.headline: Chicago's surprise rise keeps European feeds calm.

text.p: An unexpected rise in Chicago futures after USDA left 1996/97 U.S. soybean ending stocks unchanged at $125 million bushels this afternoon kept the European market subdued with only a few trades reported, market sources said.

"Most European dealers thought Chicago soybean futures would drop after USDA kept ending stocks unchanged with expectations the carryout would be maybe as much as 10 million bushels lower. But Chicago took a turn upwards over weather and export figures instead, which was enough to get everybody in Europe sidelined," one broker said.
